Auto-generated Summary (optional, may be partial):

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros from our side, I'm Ethan, AE on the account, this is Maya our SE. with you?
[00:07] Liam: hi Ethan, yeah Liam here, head of security at Argus. Priya and Jake are with me.
[00:11] Priya: hi all.
[00:12] Jake: yep, thanks.
[00:15] Ethan: great. goal today is a focused walkthrough of Redwood's data handling and retention controls — logging redaction, request storage toggles, how to meet your compliance bar. we'll show both console and API ways to do it. sound good?
[00:26] Liam: yep, high level yes. our main asks: can we prevent any PII from being stored by Redwood by default; for the pilot we need to be sure requests are not persisted and that any logs are redacted. also we need proof of deletion and an audit trail.
[00:39] Maya: totally. we'll demo the 'store_request' toggle in the Console and the equivalent API header, show automatic redaction, and how that ties to audit logs + KMS. we'll also call out limitations and fallback behaviors.
[00:49] Priya: when you say redaction, is that deterministic? like we need to know what was removed. we also have structured card numbers in payloads so masking has to be reliable.
[00:58] Maya: good question. Redwood uses a multi-stage pipeline: first a PII classifier (model-based heuristic), then deterministic regex masking for known patterns (cards, emails), and finally a manual redaction rule set per-tenant. the pipeline writes a redaction report to the audit log — the original payload is either not stored or stored encrypted under customer KMS depending on your setting.
[01:16] Jake: if we turn off storage, is there any transient storage for telemetry? like will tokens or kv cache snippets show up in logs?
[01:24] Maya: short answer: no persistent request body. transient in-memory buffers exist for inference and are not written to disk; telemetry traces (latency, token counts) are retained by default for X days but can be toggled and aggregated. if you set store_request=false on the project, the request body and model outputs are not written to our request store. we still keep minimal execution metadata for billing unless you opt into billing-redaction which we can discuss.
[01:45] Liam: billing is a concern, we need cost visibility but can't have raw card numbers out of our systems.
[01:50] Ethan: we have two patterns customers use: 1) hashed identifiers + aggregated metrics for billing, or 2) store an encrypted blob under customer KMS and rotate keys; the latter gives proof of possession but you control decryption.
[02:02] Priya: show us the console please.
[02:05] Maya: sure, sharing screen — (console noise) okay on the project settings page there's 'Data handling' section. first toggle: 'Store requests' default on for trial, but you can flip to off. when off we set store_request=false and a banner notes "no request bodies retained". you can also set a retention window: 0/7/30/90/365 days or custom.
[02:30] Maya: next is 'PII redaction' — options: automatic (model + regex), strict (apply aggressive token masking), and manual rules. you can preview redactions inline with sample payloads. here's a sample payload showing a card number — the preview shows it masked as [REDACTED-CARD].
[02:47] Jake: preview looks good but we need to see a downloadable report of redaction events for audit.
[02:52] Maya: yep — there's an 'Export Redaction Report' button that produces CSV/JSON lines with event id, redaction type, fields redacted, and a hash of original (not reversible). if you require a proof-of-deletion we can produce deletion receipts for stored blobs — signed timestamp by our service asserting deletion occurred at X.
[03:12] Liam: what's the SLA for those deletion receipts and can they be used in audits?
[03:17] Ethan: the receipts are cryptographic signatures over the deletion event, timestamped and stored in the audit log which is retained per your audit_retention policy. many customers have used these in compliance reviews; we'll share sample receipts in the security pack.
[03:28] Priya: about KMS — we run in GCP and our policy requires CMEK for any persisted data. does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[03:36] Maya: yes, we support CMEK via Cloud KMS and AWS KMS; the Console has a key binding flow and API accepts key identifier. if store_request is on, request bodies are encrypted with that key; if off, you can still opt to store an encrypted blob for forensics but you control key rotation and revocation.
[03:53] Priya: ok. can you show the API header example for toggling storage per-call?
[03:58] Maya: sure. example: X-Redwood-Store-Request: false or we expose a request param store_request=false in the JSON payload. we also have X-Redwood-Redact: aggressive to force strict pipeline. will paste these examples to the Slack thread after.
[04:13] Jake: what about model logs — like kv cache and token caches, could anything leak?
[04:18] Maya: runtime keeps KV in memory; we never persist KV to disk. debug dumps are gated behind SE ops and require justification and an audit entry. by default no debug dumps are created.
[04:29] Liam: slightly worried about third-party integrations — e.g. if we route to a fallback model in another region, how is data handled?
[04:36] Ethan: good flag. we have routing policies per project; you can restrict routing to region and deployment type (hosted vs dedicated vs private). fallback models won't be used if you disallow cross-region routing. for enterprise we recommend Dedicated or Private when you need stricter controls.
[04:51] Priya: private deployment — if we go on-prem, do you still have a control plane?
[04:56] Ethan: we offer a private control plane option where audit logs and some telemetry can be pushed to your SIEM; you manage the networking and keys. the on-prem package keeps everything inside your VPC, so no Redwood-hosted request store unless you enable it.
[05:08] Liam: are there any edge cases where PII could be reconstructed from model outputs or embeddings we store?
[05:15] Maya: embeddings can sometimes encode sensitive signals; we recommend not storing embeddings when working with raw PII unless you apply deterministic hashing or differential privacy. Console has an embeddings retention toggle and anonymization pipeline we can enable for your project.
[05:29] Jake: performance impact — does aggressive redaction add latency?
[05:33] Maya: minimal for the regex stage; model-based PII detection adds a small ms overhead per request. we can benchmark with your payloads during the pilot; typically under 10-30 ms added per call depending on payload size.
[05:45] Priya: earlier you mentioned billing-redaction opt-in. can you outline that?
[05:49] Ethan: billing-redaction routes usage events through a hash-and-aggregate pipeline so we can produce per-route token counts without storing raw request payloads. it's an additional configuration and some customers accept slightly less granularity for full payload privacy.
[06:03] Liam: legal asked about exceptions — retention windows for fraud investigations where we may need to keep a record beyond normal retention. is there a special workflow?
[06:12] Maya: yes, we have a 'retention exception' audit workflow: you request an exception via the Console (requires an authorized RBAC role), it creates an exception ticket, and retention is extended for specified objects with full audit and owner justification. exceptions are visible in the audit log and require multi-admin approval if enforced by policy.
[06:32] Jake: that helps. can we test deletion proofs during the pilot?
[06:36] Maya: absolutely — pilot runbook will include deletion proof tests: create data, enable storage, then call delete and request receipt. we'll include automated assertions.
[06:44] Priya: about SSO and RBAC — we want admin roles to manage retention.
[06:48] Ethan: we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC in the Console. roles can be scoped to projects and to specific actions (e.g., 'request_store_toggle', 'export_redaction_report', 'request_deletion').
[07:02] Liam: last question — can we get a forward-looking roadmap of features, especially HSM-backed signing for deletion receipts?
[07:09] Maya: HSM-backed signing is in roadmap Q1 next year; currently deletion receipts are signed by our service keys; we have KMS integrations though and can provide a whitepaper. we'll share roadmap notes in the security pack.
[07:21] Ethan: quick recap and next steps: we'll send SOC2 + architecture + redaction whitepaper, Maya will prepare pilot runbook and API examples including headers and sample payloads, Priya will share payloads, and we'll target pilot the week of 2026-12-20. any other items?
[07:38] Liam: no, that covers it. thanks.
[07:40] Jake: thanks, good session.
